title: Range Rover P38A
verdict: The last Range Rover with a ladder frame and beam axles, wrapped in a 1990s electronics experiment. Cheap to buy, cheap to fix yourself, and ruinously expensive to pay someone else to love.

paragraphs: Following a 24-year-old legend is a thankless job, and the P38A did it in September 1994 with a straight face. Land Rover called it the New Range Rover; everyone else named it after the office block the engineers worked in. Underneath the squarer, plusher body it was still a proper Rover: a separate steel chassis, live axles front and rear, a two-speed transfer box and the faithful aluminium V8. On top it piled self-levelling air suspension, a body computer under the right-hand front seat and enough wiring to cable a small town. Thirty years on, that split personality is exactly why it is both the bargain and the booby trap of the [[range-rover/classic|Range Rover]] family.

story.heading: PEGASUS, DISCOVERY AND BLOCK 38A
paragraphs: The project started life as "Pegasus", then wore the cover name "Discovery" to confuse snooping journalists — awkward, since Land Rover had a real [[land-rover/discovery-1|Discovery]] on sale. When the team moved into Block 38A at Solihull, the building's name stuck, and P38A it has been ever since. Inside the company it was the LP. Styling director George Thomson's in-house design was chosen over a Bertone proposal, and production at Solihull began in 1994 with sales running to the 2002 model year in the US.

It could have been very different under the bonnet. During development a pair of prototypes was fitted with BMW's 5.4-litre M73 V12 from the 750i, but the idea was shelved and never reached production. Instead buyers got the Rover V8 in 4.0 and new 4.6-litre forms, plus — outside North America — a 2.5-litre BMW M51 straight-six turbodiesel with 136 hp. The petrol V8s could be had with an R380 five-speed manual or ZF automatics; the 4.6 was automatic-only.

story.heading: AIR, ELECTRONS AND A SMARTER TRANSFER BOX
paragraphs: The headline hardware was the Electronic Air Suspension, developed from the late Classic LSE system. It offers five heights — Access, Motorway, Standard, Off-Road and an Off-Road Extended setting the computer selects on its own when it senses the truck is beached. It lowers itself at speed and lifts for obstacles, which is lovely until a perished air spring or tired compressor leaves one corner kneeling in your driveway.

The drivetrain went electronic too. The BorgWarner 4462 transfer box shifts between high and low range with an electric actuator rather than a lever, selected through an H-gate on automatic trucks and a dash switch on manuals, and the truck has to be nearly stopped to change. Traction control started out rear-only on the 4.0 and diesel, with the 4.6 getting four-wheel control; from mid-1999 the V8s switched from Lucas GEMS to Bosch Motronic engine management, and later trucks got four-wheel traction control across the range.

story.heading: WHY IT'S STILL WORTH YOUR WEEKENDS
paragraphs: Strip away the reputation and the P38 is a long-travel, beam-axle 4x4 with real low range, 3,500 kg of braked towing capacity and a 100-litre tank — a better overland base than its price suggests. The aftermarket agrees: Terrafirma makes sliders, winch bumpers, a snorkel and lift springs for it, and Lucky8 developed a 4-inch coil kit on its own P38 project truck. Converting to coils is a bolt-in job if you'd rather not carry an air compressor through the backcountry.

The flip side is that P38s are now cheap enough to be neglected. Classic magazines put good runners at a couple of thousand pounds and project cars at a few hundred, and plenty have had years of deferred maintenance. Ignore the cosmetics and buy on cooling-system health, a dry body computer and a working EAS; then budget for blend motors, heater O-rings and bushes. Do it yourself and the P38 is one of the best-value long-travel 4x4s on the road.

story.heading: THE END OF THE LADDER
paragraphs: The P38 was the last Range Rover with a separate chassis, live axles, a manual gearbox option and a classic two-speed transfer box. Its replacement, the [[range-rover/l322|L322]], was developed under BMW with a monocoque body and independent air suspension, and every Range Rover since has followed that path. For buyers who want the ladder frame, the P38 sits between the hand-tool simplicity of the [[range-rover/classic|Classic]] and the computer-dependent [[range-rover/l322|L322]]. It's the last one you can still fix with mostly analogue hardware, plus a diagnostic tool for the electronics.

callout.label: SIDEBAR · FUN FACT
callout.title: The BMW V12 Range Rover that never was
paragraphs: Somebody at Land Rover clearly wanted to know what a Range Rover would be like with a German V12. Two P38 prototypes were built with the 5.4-litre M73 V12 from the BMW 750i before the project was shelved. None reached production.

BMW's influence did make it to showrooms in a quieter form: the diesel P38 used BMW's 2.5-litre M51 turbodiesel six, and from mid-1999 the V8s ran Bosch Motronic management closely related to the system in the E38 7 Series. The next Range Rover, the L322, went much further and shared its first engines and electronics with the 7 Series.

engineering_intro: The P38 is a transitional truck: Classic-style bones with an electronic nervous system bolted on. A separate steel chassis carries two beam axles on air springs, permanent four-wheel drive runs through an electronically shifted BorgWarner two-speed transfer box, and power comes from the long-serving aluminium Rover V8 or a BMW diesel six. The mechanical parts are tough and well supported by the aftermarket. The weak spots are the systems controlling them: the EAS valve block and compressor, the climate-control blend motors and the body computer.

engineering.note: Strengthened over the Classic with new welding methods for better corrosion resistance.
EAS has five heights from Access to Off-Road Extended. Terrafirma sells bolt-in coil conversions.
GEMS management to mid-1999, Bosch Motronic after that. 4.0s tend to blow head gaskets; 4.6s tend to slip liners.
136 hp, 270 Nm. EGR and a plastic inlet manifold on post-1998 engines. Not sold in the US.
High and low range are selected electronically, and the truck has to be nearly stopped to change.
Rear-only traction control at first on the 4.0 and diesel. Four-wheel control on the 4.6 from new and on later trucks.

generations_table.note: R380 5-speed manual or ZF 4HP22 auto. Rear-only traction control at first.
ZF 4HP24 auto only. 4-pin rear diff and four-wheel traction control.
Non-US. EGR, plastic intake and a MAF sensor on post-1998 engines.
Bosch Motronic replaces Lucas GEMS mid-1999, with revised mounts and a structural sump. Four-wheel traction control on later trucks.
Clear front and rear indicators, new wheels and more standard kit. Special editions include the Holland & Holland, Westminster and Bordeaux.

buying_checks.head: Coolant history comes first
buying_checks.body: The V8's big failure is coolant loss: 4.0s usually blow head gaskets and 4.6s slip cylinder liners. The system holds roughly 11.4 litres. Check the level and condition, ask about overheating, and look up the hose and thermostat history. A properly rebuilt engine needs top-hat liners or a new block.

buying_checks.head: Look for a wet floor and a wet body computer
buying_checks.body: Damp in the passenger or driver footwell often means leaking heater matrix O-rings. Water in the cargo area or spare-wheel well points to failed tailgate seals. Remove the lower trim at the right-hand front seat (the passenger seat on US trucks) and check the Body Electrical Control Module (BECM) for water damage, because a drowned BECM is the expensive version of this problem.

buying_checks.head: Cycle the air suspension
buying_checks.body: Raise the truck to its highest setting and look at all four air springs. Listen for the compressor running constantly or cycling often, which points to leaks. An EAS warning or a lean on one corner can mean a tired height sensor. Springs are cheap from aftermarket suppliers (under £100 each), so a leak is a negotiating point, not a deal-breaker.

buying_checks.head: Read the HVAC display
buying_checks.body: A 'book' symbol on the climate-control LCD means a stored hard fault, commonly the blend motors, blower relays or A/C. Test full cold on recirculation and cycle every vent. Replacing blend motors properly means taking the dash apart, and a dealer quote can run close to $2,000.

buying_checks.head: Shift into low range
buying_checks.body: With the truck almost stopped, select low and then high again a few times. Hesitation, 'Select Neutral' or gearbox-fault messages can come from the transfer-box motor, its harness, or a misaligned XYZ gear-position switch. Listen for centre-diff clonks on tight turns.

buying_checks.head: Check rust where it hides
buying_checks.body: The panels are mostly aluminium, but rear arches are the worst cosmetic rust spot and the tailgate rusts under its plastic flap. Check the rear brake lines and look for chassis damage from off-road use.

buying_checks.head: Plug in a diagnostic tool
buying_checks.body: Check that all warning lights come on with the ignition and go out (the ABS light should go out once you drive off). A P38-capable tool such as Blackbox Solutions' Nanocom will read the EAS, BECM and HVAC fault logs that a basic OBD reader can't.

buying_checks.head: Petrol V8, and buy on condition
buying_checks.body: UK buyers' guides say choose the petrol V8 and pick on condition rather than 4.0 vs 4.6. Be wary of LPG conversions without documented professional fitting. The diesel is slow and has its own head-gasket and fuel-system issues.

repairs.title: Cooling hose and thermostat refresh (GEMS V8)
repairs.cost: About $260 for a complete hose and thermostat kit, plus coolant
repairs.symptoms: An ageing cooling system on a 4.0 or 4.6. Cracked or soft hoses, a high or overfilling expansion tank, or a heater that blows lukewarm. On these engines, overheating is what leads to slipped liners and blown head gaskets.
repairs.fix: Remove the reservoir cap and drain the system from the radiator's bottom plug with a 12 mm Allen socket. Expect roughly 11–12 litres (about 3 US gallons). The thermostat is an external 'artificial heart' unit held by its hoses next to the radiator. Replace it with the lower hose from underneath, then do the top hose, heater hoses and bypass hoses. While the hoses are off, unbolt and check the metal down-tube for rust blockage. There is no bleed screw. Fill, warm the engine fully, let it cool completely, then top up again. Run the heater to confirm the core isn't air-locked.
repairs.tools: 12 mm Allen socket on a ½-in drive · hose-clamp pliers · 5-gallon drain pan · Atlantic British kit 9369SKA (1995–99 GEMS trucks)

repairs.title: EAS valve block reseal and compressor rebuild
repairs.cost: O-ring and piston-seal kits are cheap. Most of the cost is your time
repairs.symptoms: The truck sags overnight, the compressor runs for a long time or keeps cycling, the reservoir is slow to fill, or there's an audible hiss from the valve block or silencer.
repairs.fix: Remove the valve block and compressor (the EAS box is on the left side of the engine bay). Spray soapy water over the solenoids and fittings while the system is under pressure to find the leaks. Replace the solenoid O-rings and the O-rings on the manual-inflation T-pieces and 8 mm lines. Check that each kit's O-ring sizes actually match. On the compressor, check the piston liner and seal, the reed valve and its shim, and the O-ring under the reed. Some owners also replace the thermal overload switch on the compressor board.
repairs.tools: O-ring kit · compressor piston/seal kit · soapy water · basic hand tools · Nanocom or Faultmate to read and clear EAS faults

parts.name: P38 EAS valve block seal / O-ring kit
P38 EAS compressor piston seal / rebuild kit
EAS air suspension pressure switch ANR3902 (P38)

repairs.title: Air spring replacement
repairs.cost: Aftermarket springs under £100 each. About £350 genuine
repairs.symptoms: One corner drops after parking, cracked or bulging bellows when the truck is at full height, or EAS faults that come back after you clear them.
repairs.fix: Raise the truck and support the chassis securely on stands. Never leave it resting on a deflated spring. Depressurise the spring (the system runs at about 10 bar / 150 psi), clean around the fitting, and cap the line. Release the spring's retaining clips and fixings and swap in the new spring. Lower the chassis onto it and refit the clips. Reconnect the line, reinflate, and leak-test with soapy water. Off-roaders often choose uprated springs such as Arnott's Gen III.
repairs.tools: Jack and axle stands · line caps · eye protection · soapy water · diagnostic tool if faults are logged

parts.name: Dunlop front air spring set REB101740 (P38)
ANR1220 air spring retaining clip set (P38)

repairs.title: Heater matrix O-rings (wet footwell)
repairs.cost: O-rings are pennies. A new matrix runs from about £60 (Bearmach) to about £400 (genuine Valeo)
repairs.symptoms: Wet carpet beside the transmission tunnel that smells or tastes sweet, a misting windscreen, or a coolant level that keeps dropping.
repairs.fix: Start with the O-rings at the matrix pipe connection, which go brittle after 15–20 years. Owners report the pipes come out without removing the dash. The retaining screw is often seized, so put grinding paste on the screwdriver tip, or drill the head off if you have to. Don't overtighten on reassembly, because the joint has to move with heat. If the matrix itself leaks, replacing it means pulling the dash and console. Pressure-test the old and new cores at about 20 psi, and test them hot. Clear the drain under the core while you're in there.
repairs.tools: Screwdrivers · drill · grinding paste · new O-rings · Nissens 70220/70230 or equivalent matrix if replacing

repairs.title: Blend motor diagnosis
repairs.cost: Motors come pre-wired in a three-pack. Owners quote dealer repairs close to $2,000
repairs.symptoms: Hot air on one side and cold on the other, a 'book' symbol on the climate display, or temperature that doesn't change.
repairs.fix: Do the cheap checks first: blower and blend-motor relays, clogged pollen filters, and coolant level and bleeding. If a motor runs on direct voltage but won't move its flap, the flap may be jammed by a warped plenum, or the motor's internal potentiometer may be worn. Owners use a Nanocom's 'calibrate flaps' function after fitting new motors. As a winter stopgap, one owner unplugged a dead motor and set its flap open by hand.
repairs.tools: Multimeter · relays · pollen filters · Nanocom/Faultmate · replacement motors

repairs.title: XYZ gear-position switch alignment
repairs.cost: About $100 for the alignment tool, plus a switch if yours has failed
repairs.symptoms: 'Select Neutral' or gearbox-fault messages during range changes, wrong gear indication, or the transfer box refusing to change range.
repairs.fix: The transmission ECU reads the transfer-box motor position as a Gray code, so check the motor harness and its earth first. Then check the XYZ (inhibitor/gear-position) switch on the auto gearbox. Set it with the dealer alignment tool LRT-44-011 rather than by eye. Atlantic British has reissued that tool and published a video of the procedure.
repairs.tools: XYZ switch alignment tool LRT-44-011 · multimeter · diagnostic tool

repairs.title: Front suspension bushes and ball joints
repairs.time: 4–6 hours for all four ball joints
repairs.symptoms: Vague steering, wander, clonks over bumps, uneven tyre wear. The front usually wears out first.
repairs.fix: Replace the radius arm bushes and the swivel ball joints, which need a special press tool. Polyurethane bush kits such as Polybush are popular. Use poly at both ends of the truck, and don't put poly in the Panhard rod. Check the dampers, drop links and ABS sensors while you're there.
repairs.tools: Ball-joint press · breaker bar · bush kit (e.g. Polybush radius-arm-to-axle kit)

parts.name: Lemförder upper & lower ball joint set ×4 (FTC3570/FTC3571)
P38 front radius arm bush kit
Polybush P38 front radius arm-to-axle kit (Comfort)

faq.q: What's the biggest tire I can fit without a lift?
faq.a: Forum reports say 245/75R16 or 255/70R16, roughly 30 to 30.5 inches. One owner runs 255/70R16 on standard suspension with no rubbing. Another found 245/75R16 clears at full lock at standard and high ride heights, but rubs at the lowest height and can touch the back of the arch at full compression. 265/75R16 (about 31.6 in) rubs when the axles cross up unless you lift the truck and fit an adjustable Panhard rod.

faq.q: What fuel economy should I expect?
faq.a: Poor. The EPA rated a 2000 4.0 automatic at 12 mpg city, 16 highway and 13 combined, and the 4.6 at 11/14/12. The tank holds 100 litres (about 26 US gallons).

faq.q: How much can a P38 tow?
faq.a: 3,500 kg (7,716 lb) braked and 750 kg unbraked, according to published spec sheets for the 4.6 HSE.

Buy the better truck. Buyers' guides say choose on condition rather than displacement. The 4.0 is more likely to blow a head gasket and the 4.6 more likely to slip a liner, so cooling-system history matters more than size. The 4.6 has more power, a 4-pin rear diff and four-wheel traction control from new. It came only with the ZF automatic.

faq.q: Which years are the best to buy?
faq.a: Hagerty's advice is to buy on condition and specification rather than age, adding that the electrical faults that dogged these trucks are now understood and fixable. ReRev says 1998 drew the most complaints of any Range Rover year on CarComplaints. Mid-1999-on V8s have Bosch Motronic instead of GEMS, but no guide we found says that alone makes them the better buy; cooling-system history matters more.

faq.q: Do I have a GEMS or a Bosch engine?
faq.a: Open the hood. A rectangular plenum with '4.0' or '4.6' embossed in the middle means GEMS, the earlier Lucas system. A cluster of intake tubes and no label means Bosch Motronic, which arrived mid-1999. The two use different parts, so check before ordering.

faq.q: Does it have low range and locking diffs?
faq.a: It has full-time four-wheel drive with a two-speed BorgWarner 4462 transfer box, switched electrically. Slow almost to a stop before changing range. There are no factory locking diffs; traction control brakes a spinning wheel instead (rear-only on early 4.0 and diesel trucks, all four wheels on the 4.6 and on later trucks). For bigger tyres, Ashcroft makes heavy-duty 4.10 ring-and-pinion sets for the P38's diffs.

faq.q: Should I convert to coil springs?
faq.a: It's a common way to simplify the truck. Terrafirma's standard-height kit TF223 is a bolt-in swap. Before you do it, note that air springs are cheap now and leaks are often just perished seals that are easy to fix. UK guides say coil conversions are becoming less popular as EAS parts get cheaper, and a healthy EAS gives you the extra off-road height.

Lucky8's 4-inch kit (Terrafirma heavy-duty springs, +2-in Pro Sport shocks, mounting plates and an EAS override harness) was developed on its own P38 project truck. Lucky8 recommends tyres up to 32.5 in with it. Owners also report about 2 in of lift from Arnott Gen III air springs with Terrafirma shocks. Bigger lifts usually need double-cardan driveshafts (Tom Wood's) to cure vibration, and adjustable Panhard rods to re-centre the axles.

faq.q: Is the BMW diesel worth having?
faq.a: It's the economy choice outside the US: a 2.5-litre BMW M51 six with 136 hp and 270 Nm. UK buyers' guides still recommend the petrol V8 and warn about diesel head gaskets (especially on remapped trucks), glow plugs and fuel-system parts. It was never sold in North America.

faq.q: What maintenance gets skipped that I shouldn't skip?
faq.a: Coolant hoses and thermostat: Land Rover's schedule says every 90,000 miles. Automatic gearbox oil about every 70,000 miles. The V8's mass airflow sensor at about 90,000 miles. Ignition leads, which wear quickly on the V8. The EAS compressor filter.

faq.q: Why does the driver's or passenger's footwell get wet?
faq.a: Usually the heater matrix O-rings, or a blocked drain under the heater box. Sometimes it's a leaking matrix. Clogged drains and failed seals can also let water reach the body computer under the seat, so fix wet carpets quickly.

mods.why: Lucky8's Terrafirma-based 4-inch coil kit was proven on its P38 'Rhino' project truck and clears tyres up to about 32.5 in. Owners who want to keep air springs run Arnott Gen III springs with longer shocks.
A bolt-in standard-height kit takes the compressor, valve block and air springs out of the equation for remote travel.
Lifted P38s run steeper driveshaft angles, which causes vibration and wears out U-joints. Double-cardan shafts fix it.

who.name: Tom Wood's P38 double-cardan shafts (via Lucky8)

mods.why: Steel sliders with tree bars, a winch-ready front bumper and a heavy-duty rear bumper to replace the plastic one.
Bigger tyres blunt the V8. Heavy-duty 4.10 ring-and-pinion sets restore acceleration and strengthen the diffs.
A snorkel raises the air intake for wading and dust. An alloy radiator helps keep a hard-working V8 away from liner-slipping temperatures.
Fresh polyurethane radius-arm bushes and a Terrafirma steering damper tighten up a tired front end.

baseline_service.intro: The P38 rewards a full catch-up service more than almost any other Range Rover. Overheating causes the V8's slipped liners, and neglected EAS and gearbox fluid cause most of the expensive failures. Change every fluid, refresh the cooling system, and leak-test the air suspension before you trust it. Note whether the engine is a GEMS (1995–98) or Bosch (1999–2002) V8, because some parts differ.

items.spec: API SG/SH or ACEA A2:96, SAE 5W-40 or 5W-50 · ≈5.8 L drain & refill (6.6 L dry)
items.note: Check the dipstick for mayonnaise and the expansion tank for oil. Either one points to head-gasket or liner trouble.

items.spec: OE-type engine air element, plus the pollen/cabin filter pair
items.note: Clogged pollen filters affect the climate control and can look like a blend-motor fault (see repairs).

items.spec: Plug type and gap per manual [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]
items.interval: At purchase if there's no record
items.note: Misfires on Bosch trucks often come from the leads and coils. Replace the plugs and leads as a set.

items.spec: V8: OE-type EFI filter [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]. 2.5 DSE diesel: STC2827
items.note: Do the diesel filter at purchase on non-US 2.5 DSE trucks.

items.spec: 50/50 ethylene glycol antifreeze and water · ≈11.4 L
items.note: Replace the hoses, thermostat and expansion-tank cap as a set (see repairs). There's no bleed screw. Warm the engine, let it cool, then top up.

items.spec: Dexron III ATF · ≈11 L total fill (4HP24 figure; 4HP22 [CONFIRM IN MANUAL]). A drain and refill takes about 5 L
items.interval: Drain and refill at purchase. Repeat after a few hundred miles
items.note: An owner on rangerovers.pub measured about 5 L from a drain and refill. Two drain-and-fills refresh most of the fluid without the risk of a flush.

items.spec: Dexron III ATF · ≈2.0 L drain & refill (2.4 L dry)
items.note: Range-change faults ('Select Neutral') are usually electrical or an XYZ switch problem, not low oil. See repairs.

parts.name: P38 transfer box drain/fill plugs and seals

items.spec: Hypoid gear oil, API GL-5 [CONFIRM grade IN MANUAL] · ≈1.6 L each drain & refill (1.7 L dry)
items.note: Fill to the level plug on level ground. Check the pinion seals.

items.spec: Sealed ball joints. There's no swivel oil or grease to change
items.note: Unlike the Classic and Defender, the P38 front axle uses press-fit ball joints. Check them for play while the wheels are off.
Check the steering box and the PAS cooler pipes for weeps.
An ABS pump that keeps running, or ABS warnings, need diagnosis with a Nanocom or a similar tool.

items.spec: System runs at about 10 bar / 150 psi. No fluid
items.interval: Leak-test at purchase. Drain any water from the reservoir and check the dryer
items.note: Park overnight at normal height and check each corner in the morning. Spray soapy water on the springs and valve block to find leaks (see repairs). Never work under a truck resting on deflated springs.

parts.name: P38 EAS air dryer and valve block seals

items.note: Inspect the tensioner and idler pulleys while the belt is off.
Grease the UJs and sliding joints. Worn UJs feel like a clunk on take-up.
